text.p: The candidate of Mongolia's ex-communist opposition People's Revolutionary Party (MPRP) was elected president, ousting President Punsalmaagiin Ochirbat, election officials said on Monday.
"You can understand that Bagabandi has won," Election Committee chairman Lhagvasuren told reporters.
Preliminary results showed Natsagiin Bagabandi, 47, had won 60.79 percent of the vote, far exceeding opinion poll forecasts.
President Ochirbat, candidate of the ruling Democratic Union Coalition, collected 29.8 percent of the vote, the committee chairman said.
A third presidential candidate, Jambin Gombojav, 56, a member of parliament running on a Mongolian Traditional United Party ticket, took just 6.6 percent of the vote, the chairman said.
Final results were expected only after vote-counting was completed in remote rural areas, Lhagvasuren said, adding that he expected little change in the final figures.
